findings.finding: Open, effective supply that can be drawn on 2026-10-01: a Roth Capital ATM of up to $4.353m under an effective S-3, and White Lion convertible notes (about $1.2m outstanding at 06-30 plus a $555,556 note of 07-10) converting at 90% of market, at an issuer holding $0.887m unrestricted cash at 06-30 against $11.1m of six-month operating cash use, which has borrowed $1.75m in demand notes from its CEO's affiliate in $100k-$500k tranches.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Nothing has to be announced first. The ATM is live (S-3 effective 2026-07-01, 424B5 of 2026-08-13 with Roth) and sells into any session, including 2026-10-01. The White Lion note converts at 90% of the market price, so the holder is a structural seller into any bounce. The issuer has done this before: 1,853,340 shares were issued on a White Lion conversion in Q2 2026, and there was a White Lion equity line in 2024. The cash position means the draw is a need, not an option.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-01 — every session the ATM and the convert are open; next ATM usage disclosure is the 10-Q, outside the window
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: the five comparable drops since the pump (09-17, 09-18, 09-21, 09-23, 09-29) were followed by -16.51, -18.43, -1.10, -5.59 and -13.60 at the next close, all negative. The seven June-August drops before the pump were mostly flat to slightly positive (+0.57, +1.56, +0.97, 0.00, +1.63, +3.00, -5.00).
findings.why_not_priced: The close prices what has been sold so far. It does not price tomorrow's ATM or conversion sales, which are undisclosed until the next 10-Q, sit on a stock still about 38% above its pre-term-sheet level (run_up_20d +38.9%), and come from an issuer that cannot fund Q4 without them. If the price held this supply, it would already show a stabilising low-volume tape after six down days. Instead each bounce has been sold.
